title: whPRI-Secure AEAD from Generic Composition
summary: Single-key SIV is suggested as a plausible publicly indifferentiable route, but whether generic composition can yield whPRI-secure AEAD remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether a $\mathrm{whPRI}$-secure AEAD scheme can be constructed by a generic composition. In particular, determine whether the single-key $\mathrm{SIV}$ composition is publicly indifferentiable when its tag-generation function is a completely random function, its conventional-encryption component is a family of $\mathrm{VIL}$ random permutations, and the same key is used for both components.

scope.domain: Generic authenticated-encryption composition, centered on single-key SIV, whPRI security, and public indifferentiability.
assumptions: The tag-generation function is a completely random function.
The conventional-encryption component is a family of VIL random permutations.
The same key is used for tag generation and conventional encryption.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a generic composition can yield a whPRI-secure AEAD scheme and, specifically, whether the stated single-key SIV composition is publicly indifferentiable.

citations.label: A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs

progress.summary: The paper explicitly raises generic construction of whPRI-secure AEAD as a natural question. It suggests that single-key SIV may be publicly indifferentiable in the stated model but provides no proof.
citation_labels: Akinori Hosoyamada et al., A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs
